title: Market Day
sub: A small game about why people buy. You mind a stall at a hill market for a day, choose what the chalkboard says, and five villagers decide.
description: Market Day: a small browser game by Riya Dutta. Mind a hill-market stall, pick the sign, and learn why each villager buys or walks away.
facts: A game in the browser, nothing to download
One chalkboard sign in the morning, one chance to change it at lunch
The idea, the villagers, the drawing and the rules
One HTML file: every tree, stall and villager drawn in SVG

hero.alt: Riya waving beside her market stall of honey jars, apples, a woollen cap and a shawl, with a chalkboard that says Fresh this morning

sections.title: Pick a sign, open up.
sections.note: Tap the chalkboard to choose what it says, then open the stall. At lunch you can change the sign once. At dusk, the ledger shows who bought and why.

items.t: Most of marketing is a nudge, not a price cut. Here you can watch five of them work on five shoppers, one at a time.
Nobody is scored on what they spent. The ledger shows the reason behind each sale, and what would have changed a no.

tiles.d: Pip the goat falls for the decoy: the big ₹400 jar makes the medium one look cheap. Kiko the yak is anchored by the ₹900 shawl.
Juno the monal only hurries when stock is short. Nell the pika follows a crowd, or a sign that says everyone else already chose.
Wren the red panda wants to know where it was made. Local wins her over.

paras: The rest of this site is work for clients. The Lab is for things I make because I want them to exist. This one turns the ideas I use every day into a morning at a hill market. A perfect day is possible, but it takes the right sign at the right time.
